## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`m0003_drop_legacy_email` must be fixed before merge: it drops a column without the backup that every destructive migration in this codebase takes, so the `legacy_email` data can't be recovered once it runs.

## Changes
The pull request adds migration 3, which drops `users.legacy_email`, and migration 4, which backs up `orders` and then drops `orders.coupon_code`. It also extends `tests/test_migrations.py` to run all four migrations in sequence.

## Critical
- migrations/m0003_drop_legacy_email.py:7 — correctness — Call backup_table before dropping legacy_email — Running `upgrade` on a `users` table with data drops `legacy_email` without first creating `users_backup_3`. `migrations/safety.py:3-5` says "each destructive migration first calls backup_table", and both m0002 and m0004 do this. — The legacy_email values are lost for good, and `restore_table(conn, "users", 3)` has no backup table to read from. — Fix: Add `backup_table(conn, "users", VERSION)` before the `ALTER TABLE`, as `migrations/m0002_drop_nickname.py:7` does, and extend `test_drop_retired_columns` to check `users_backup_3`.
